chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl also, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

When you place him in his niche-grave, then say: In the Name of Allah, and in the way of Allah, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. O Allah, Your servant has descended with You, and You are the best with whom one descends. O Allah, make spacious for him in his grave and join him to his Prophet. O Allah, we know nothing of him but good, and You are more knowing of him.

Then when you place the bricks over him, say: O Allah, keep company with his loneliness, give intimacy to his estrangement, and settle upon him from Your mercy a mercy by which You make him free of needing the mercy of anyone besides You.
Then when you depart from his grave, say: “Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return” ... “And all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
O Allah, raise his rank in the highest ʿIlliyyīn, and succeed him among those who remain behind, and with You do we reckon him, O Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.اللَّبِنَ: the bricks or slabs placed over the deceased in the grave
key_terms.رَحْمَتِكَ: Your mercy, the divine mercy sought for the deceased
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: the highest exalted stations, referring to an elevated rank in the hereafter
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave, the burial place of the deceased
key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his niche-grave, the side chamber within the grave in which the deceased is placed
key_terms.مِلَّةِ: the religious way or creed, here the faith of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.وَحْشَتَهُ: his estrangement or loneliness, especially in the grave

ai.seo_question: What supplications should be recited when burying a deceased person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the supplications to be recited at different moments of burial: when placing the deceased in the grave, when setting the bricks over him, and when leaving the grave. It emphasizes entrusting the deceased to Allah, asking for mercy, companionship in the grave, elevation of rank, and remembering the return to Allah.
